derivation: Generated by tools/import_kicad_board.py from the vendor's own KiCad footprint. Pad centres are exact to three decimal places in millimetres, scaled at 8.0 px/mm from a 24.54 x 20.75 mm extent including a 1.0 mm margin. Pin names joined from the symbol library on pad number. Nothing here was measured off an image.
assumption: Every `pin` is null: that field is the rcontrol pin index of a PICSimLab board implementation (webui/pinmap.py), and none exists for this board. `chip_pin` and `chip_index` are null on 33 of these 35 pads, because no board-support package covers this board at all -- no Zephyr board and no vendor core publishes a STM32C5 XIAO (OH-26). The other 2 were read from the vendor's own CAD, named in `pindefs`, which is a schematic and not firmware: it names a pin beside those pad names and beside no others. Each null pad says which of the two it is in its own `why_null`. The pin view reports every null pad as not modelled, and will until the vendor publishes something to read. 2 pins on this board are named with NO flat number -- PA13, PA14 -- so every pad reaching one carries `chip_index` null for that reason and not for a missing reading: no flat GPIO numbering is published for the STM32C5 at all, so a module for it would key its own table the way webui/boards/samd21.py does, and until one exists no level is read for any pad here.

pindefs.derivation: Generated by tools/import_pindefs.py, which found no board-support package covering this board. Anything named in `packages` is a source read anyway -- the vendor's own CAD rather than firmware -- and resolves a pad only where it names the pin outright. Every pad it does not reach is null and says why in its own `why_null`.
